title: Carry a trapped interlock key from a breaker to the matching door
instruction: Both breakers are open. Turn key A1 a quarter turn in breaker A1's interlock to lock that breaker open and free the key. Then take key A1 to the interlock on fuse compartment door A1, insert it, and turn it a quarter turn to unlock the door. Use only the locks marked A1.
context: Trapped-key interlocks make workers open a breaker before they can reach the compartment it feeds. The sequence is only safe if the key freed at the breaker goes to the door with the same code; using the wrong lock, or forcing a door, puts a worker in front of live parts.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Both arms start at the ready pose with grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Two interlock pairs, A1 on the left and B1 on the right; each pair has its own labels (A1 safety yellow, B1 light blue, black lettering). Breaker A1: a molded-case circuit breaker stand-in sized like a Square D PowerPact H-frame 3-pole breaker (dark grey plastic box 10.5 cm deep, 16 cm wide, 8.6 cm tall), lying face up and fixed to the table, its centre 17 cm in front of the bases and 40 cm left of the midline, long side left-right. Its toggle handle (2.2 x 1.2 cm, 3.2 cm tall) tilts 20 degrees each way about a front-back axis: OFF leans left, ON leans right; it is at OFF, held there by an over-centre detent (0.5 N m). A yellow label 3.4 x 8.4 cm reading A1 is on its face between the robot-side edge and the handle, and a 15 x 7 cm one on its robot-facing side. A Kirk Type F key interlock (SD series, single cylinder; brass housing 44.5 x 63.5 x 34.9 mm, cylinder 34.5 mm across; stainless 5/8 in (15.9 mm) bolt with a 3/4 in (19 mm) throw; red nameplate engraved A1) is bracketed to the breaker's far edge on a steel bracket, cylinder face up, keyway 22.2 cm in front of the bases, 38.9 cm left of the midline and 14.6 cm above the table. Its bolt is withdrawn; when extended it stands in the handle's path 2 mm on the ON side, 2.2 cm above the breaker face. Key A1 is in this lock, trapped: a nickel-silver key stand-in with a 28 x 24 x 3 mm bow stamped A1 on a yellow patch (bow upright, its centre 2.1 cm above the cylinder face), a 6 x 6 mm square shank and a 5 mm bit; 20 g. Breaker B1, its interlock (nameplate B1) and key B1: identical, with blue labels, centre 17 cm in front of the bases and 40 cm right of the midline, handle at OFF, keyway 22.2 cm in front and 41.1 cm right of the midline; key B1 has a 4 x 7.6 mm flat shank instead of the square one and is trapped in breaker B1's interlock. Door A1: a fuse compartment door stand-in, a grey-painted 3 mm steel plate (10 cm wide, 14 cm tall, 0.3 kg) standing upright and facing the robot, its front face 34 cm in front of the bases, spanning 11 to 21 cm left of the midline, bottom edge 3 mm above the table, hinged on its left edge to a light grey box (9 cm deep, 11 cm wide, 15.2 cm tall) behind it. It has a black handle (1.3 x 1.2 x 3 cm) 12-13.2 cm left of the midline and 8.5-11.5 cm above the table, a label FUSE COMPT. A1 on its face, and a yellow 7.6 x 10 cm label reading A1 on the box's top. A second Kirk Type F (nameplate A1, no key in it) is fixed on the table in front of the door's lower right corner, cylinder up, keyway 29 cm in front of the bases, 7 cm left of the midline and 5.4 cm above the table; its bolt is extended through an 18 mm square hole in a steel keeper tab on the door, so the door is locked shut. Door B1: identical, labelled FUSE COMPT. B1 with a blue top label, spanning 6 to 16 cm right of the midline, its interlock (nameplate B1, no key, bolt extended) with keyway 29 cm in front and 20 cm right of the midline. All four interlocks turn the same way: a quarter turn counterclockwise seen from above extends the bolt, a quarter turn clockwise withdraws it. A key can be pulled out only with its lock's bolt extended. The key codes differ: key A1 enters only the A1 locks and key B1 only the B1 locks.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time before the after-release check: a key's tip is brought within 12 mm of the keyway axis of a lock with the other code (and less than 10 mm above its face); either B1 interlock (on breaker B1 or on door B1) is turned 10 degrees or more; a finger comes within 1.5 cm of a door's handle while that door is still bolted, or a bolted door moves 3 degrees or more; or either breaker's handle moves 5 degrees or more toward ON. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if breaker A1's interlock bolt is extended 18 mm or more with key A1 in it; 0.5 if key A1 is also out of that lock (its tip 2 mm or more above the cylinder face, or 2 cm or more to the side of the keyway); 0.75 if key A1 is also inserted in door A1's interlock (tip within 3 mm of the keyway axis and 8 mm or more below the face) and turned so that door's bolt is within 4 mm of fully withdrawn; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. Dropping a key is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from key A1's bow for 1 s: (1) pull key A1 straight up with a spring scale at 5 N for 1.5 s; pass if it rises less than 3 mm; (2) push breaker A1's handle toward ON at 50 N applied 3 cm above its pivot (1.5 N m) for 1.5 s; pass if it stays at least 5 degrees on the OFF side of its middle position; (3) pull door A1's handle straight toward the robot at 3.5 N (about 0.3 N m about the hinge) for 1.5 s; pass if the door opens past 20 degrees. All three must pass for 1.0; otherwise the score stays 0.75. Distances are read with a rule, angles from a photo taken from above.
reset_notes: Shut door A1 and turn key A1 a quarter turn counterclockwise so its bolt goes through the keeper; pull key A1 out, put it back into breaker A1's interlock and turn it a quarter turn clockwise to withdraw that bolt, which traps the key. Check both breaker handles are at OFF, key B1 is in breaker B1's interlock with its bolt withdrawn, and door B1 is bolted shut. If a run ended with a B1 lock turned, undo that the same way. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Interlocking is geometry: the key turns a plug whose crank moves the bolt (stand-in for Kirk's unpublished cam); key trapped until the bolt is out; the bolt jams the breaker handle. Coding is warded (a wrong key cannot turn). Stand-in keys; generic breakers, doors laid face up as a bench mock-up; colour labels ours. Turning resistance is damping; release check applied in sim after recording. Details in README.
